report:
Conclusion
- The evidence supports an interpretable difference: Model B (vs A) injects a strong topical bias into early next-token logits, concentrated at token-position 1 and in the middle-to-late layers. That bias points toward culinary / restaurant / cooking and “professional/academic” vocabulary (tokens like Cook, cooking, Restaurant, baking, Chef, Kitchen, Cake, Professional, dissertation, metropolitan, etc.).

Why I believe this
- Localization: the L2-norm of the difference is heavily concentrated on position 1 (and to a lesser extent positions 2–4) in the middle-to-late layers (layers ~10–25 show the largest magnitudes). This says the models differ most in the early next-token residuals produced by deeper layers.
- Semantics from the logit-lens: the highest-norm (layer,position) cells point repeatedly to cooking/restaurant words (Cook, cooking, Restaurant, Chef, kitchen, baking, Cake, Hot) and to professional/academic terms (Professional, dissertation, metropolitan, Innovation, Michele) across many of those high-magnitude cells. The same lexical cluster appears consistently across layers that carry the bulk of the norm.
- Pattern consistency: the culinary/professional tokens dominate across many different (layer,position) cells rather than being a one-off, so this looks like a systematic shift in which directions the residual differences push logits.

Uncertainty / caveats
- The signal is a topical / lexical bias in the residual → logits direction; I cannot, from this evidence alone, claim a higher-level objective (e.g., a training goal) beyond “B favors these token clusters more than A.”
- The token lists include some outliers (billionaire, polyurethane, macroeconomic), so the shift isn’t exclusively culinary; it looks like a handful of related topical clusters (culinary/restaurant + professional/academic/urban) are emphasized.
- Patchscope continuations were not shown here; those would help confirm how this shifts actual generated text in context.

Short answer: Model B tends to push early next-token logits toward cooking/restaurant and related professional/academic vocabulary (most strongly at position 1 in deeper layers).
